papers.title: Oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembled nanoparticles alleviate neurological injury after ischemic stroke via the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β axis.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability, while the current clinically applicable adjunctive neuroprotective strategies face substantial limitations. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin exhibit synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities; however, their poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability remain major limitations to their therapeutic development. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin were formulated as co-assembled nanoparticles using an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. A 5:2 mass ratio of oleanolic acid to hesperetin produce
papers.summary: This study formulates oleanolic acid and hesperetin into co-assembled nanoparticles to overcome their poor solubility and bioavailability, and tests whether the formulation protects against neurological injury after ischemic stroke. The authors report that the nanoparticles alleviate neurological damage via modulation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β signaling axis. The work is a preclinical drug-delivery and neuroprotection study rather than a genomics or bioinformatics resource.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of hybrid molecules combining paracetamol with thiazole derivatives via hydrazone or azo linkers, aiming to create dual-acting COX inhibitors with immunomodulatory activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking supporting the design rationale.

papers.title: Revealing protein structural transitions in the era of generative artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence and deep generative models have greatly accelerated the generation of protein conformational ensembles. Moving beyond isolated structural states to reconstruct continuous, physically realistic transition pathways further provides mechanistic understanding to guide molecular design but remains a significant challenge. This review examines emerging computational approaches for modeling protein conformational transitions, from classical molecular dynamics simulations to deep learning-based latent space interpolation. Recent developments in capturing natu
papers.summary: This review surveys computational methods for modeling protein conformational transitions, spanning classical molecular dynamics to deep learning-based latent space interpolation. It highlights how generative AI now enables generation of protein conformational ensembles and discusses the challenge of reconstructing continuous, physically realistic transition pathways for mechanistic understanding and molecular design.

papers.title: A recyclable [DABCO][Imi]2 deep eutectic solvent for multicomponent synthesis of 1,2-dihydropyridine-3-carbonitriles: in vitro antiproliferative and in silico molecular evaluation.
papers.abstract: This study reports the synthesis of a novel deep eutectic solvent (DES), [DABCO][Imi]2, for the multicomponent synthesis of 2-oxo-4,6-disubstituted-1,2-dihydropyridine-3-carbonitrile derivatives. A novel DES was successfully synthesized and structurally characterized using 1H NMR, 13C NMR, FT-IR spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). A series of 30 derivatives was synthesized in moderate isolated yields (up to 40%). The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against human melanoma A375 cancer cells. Among the synthesized compounds, (5cg) and (5ch) exhib
papers.summary: The authors developed a new deep eutectic solvent, [DABCO][Imi]2, and used it as a recyclable reaction medium for multicomponent synthesis of 1,2-dihydropyridine-3-carbonitrile derivatives. Thirty compounds were made in modest yields (up to 40%), and two of them showed antiproliferative activity against human melanoma A375 cells, supported by in silico molecular docking. The work is primarily a synthetic chemistry/methodology contribution with preliminary anticancer evaluation.

papers.title: Selection of novel activators of non-genomic estrogen-like signaling (ANGELS) with promising potential for Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common type of dementia, affecting elderly women two- to threefold more than similar aged man, or the younger generations. Although 17β-estradiol offers neuroprotection, its clinical use is limited by serious side effects. This study explored a molecular group called ANGELS (Activators of Non-Genomic Estrogen-Like Signaling) as safer alternatives. A steroid library was screened via computational docking to estrogen receptor α. The top binders were preselected via in vitro and in vivo tests. The neuroprotective effect was examined in two mouse models of AD (
papers.summary: This study used computational docking to screen a steroid library for novel ANGELS (Activators of Non-Genomic Estrogen-Like Signaling) compounds binding estrogen receptor α, then validated top candidates in vitro and in two mouse models of Alzheimer's disease. The goal is to find estrogen-like neuroprotective agents that avoid the serious side effects of 17β-estradiol, potentially offering safer AD therapeutics, especially for women who are disproportionately affected.

papers.title: Toxicological Effects of Polyethylene Terephthalate Microplastics on Chronic Kidney Disease: An Integrative Bioinformatics, Network Toxicology, and Machine Learning Study.
papers.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are widely distributed in human organs, including the kidney, brain, and liver, where they induce oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. However, the toxicological effects of MNPs on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we employed an integrated approach combining bioinformatics, network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking to investigate the potential impacts of polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET-MPs) on CKD. A total of 191 CKD-related targets were obtained from the GEO database, while 875
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study integrates bioinformatics, network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking to predict how polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET-MPs) may affect chronic kidney disease. The authors identify CKD-related targets from GEO data and intersect them with predicted PET-MP toxicity targets, using machine learning and docking to prioritize candidate genes and mechanisms. It is a computational, hypothesis-generating analysis rather than an experimental validation of toxicological effects.

papers.title: Competing Isomerization Channels and Rotor Selectivity in a Third-Generation Molecular Motor: Insights from Nonadiabatic Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Third-generation light-driven molecular motors, characterized by a unique double-rotor architecture, represent a pivotal advancement in nanotechnology. Recently, a novel third-generation molecular motor based on bridged-isoindigo has been proposed. However, the microscopic mechanism behind its ultrafast photoisomerization remains to be explored. In this work, nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations at the semiempirical OM2/MRCI level were employed to investigate the excited-state dynamics of a third-generation molecular motor, starting from the E S Z S configuration. The simulation reveals
papers.summary: This study uses nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the ultrafast photoisomerization mechanism of a third-generation light-driven molecular motor based on bridged-isoindigo. The simulations reveal competing isomerization channels and rotor selectivity starting from the E S Z S configuration, providing microscopic insight into how the double-rotor architecture controls directional motion.

papers.title: Antibacterial Activity of Equisetin from Endophytic Fusarium incarnatum JMB4 Associated with Jatropha multifida L. Against MRSA: Experimental and In Silico Insights.
papers.abstract: An antibacterial metabolite was isolated from the endophytic fungus Fusarium incarnatum JMB4 associated with Jatropha multifida L. by bioactivity-guided chromatography and recrystallization. The isolated compound was assigned as equisetin using UV-vis, FTIR, LC-MS/MS, and 1H NMR data. Anti-MRSA activity was evaluated by disk diffusion, with chloramphenicol and amoxicillin as antibiotic comparators. At 1% (w/v; 100 μg/disk), equisetin produced an inhibition zone of 23.94 ± 0.66 mm; the recorded comparator zones were 24.71 ± 0.68 mm for chloramphenicol (30 μg/disk) and 11.76 ± 0.66 mm for amoxic
papers.summary: Researchers isolated equisetin, an antibacterial compound, from a fungus (Fusarium incarnatum JMB4) living inside the medicinal plant Jatropha multifida. Equisetin showed strong activity against MRSA, producing an inhibition zone (23.94 mm) comparable to the antibiotic chloramphenicol (24.71 mm) in disk diffusion assays. The study combines experimental isolation with computational (in silico) analysis to support the compound's anti-MRSA potential.

papers.title: Effects of Coal Rank on the Adsorption Characteristics and Mechanism of Hydrogen Sulfide by Coal Molecules.
papers.abstract: This study systematically investigates the molecular structural characteristics of different rank coals (anthracite, bituminous, lignite) and their adsorption properties and mechanisms toward hydrogen sulfide (H2S). By combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and solid-state 13C NMR spectroscopy, it was found that aromatic carbon content increases remarkably from 55.91 to 91.75% with coal rank increasing, whereas aliphatic carbon and oxygen-bearing functional groups decrease accordingly. Macromolecular model representatives corresponding to each coal rank were constructed based on expe
papers.summary: The study characterizes how coal rank (lignite, bituminous, anthracite) affects H2S adsorption by combining XPS and solid-state 13C NMR to quantify structural changes, finding aromatic carbon rises from 55.91% to 91.75% with rank while aliphatic and oxygen-bearing groups decline. Molecular models for each rank were then built to explain the adsorption mechanism. The work links coal macromolecular structure to H2S uptake behavior.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning has been applied across amyloid research, from predicting which protein sequences are likely to form amyloid fibrils to modeling their structures and designing inhibitor drugs. It argues that ML has become a transformative framework for tackling these disease-relevant polypeptides, which are central to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases.

papers.title: Hydrophobic Hydration at Fluorinated and Hydrocarbon Self-Assembled Monolayers Investigated by In Situ Soft X-Ray Emission Spectroscopy and Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: We investigated the hydrogen-bonding state and spatial distribution of water at hydrophobic self-assembled monolayer (SAM) interfaces formed by fluoroalkyl and hydrocarbon chains using in situ soft X-ray emission spectroscopy (XES) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under controlled humidity conditions. Under low water coverage, the hydrocarbon-based SAM exhibited spectral features attributed to isolated water molecules, while the fluorinated SAM showed signatures indicative of tetrahedrally coordinated hydrogen-bond networks. MD simulations revealed that water molecules at the fluorinate
papers.journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
papers.summary: This study uses soft X-ray emission spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations to compare how water organizes at fluorinated versus hydrocarbon self-assembled monolayer surfaces. At low water coverage, hydrocarbon surfaces show isolated water molecules, while fluorinated surfaces promote tetrahedrally coordinated hydrogen-bond networks. The work reveals that fluorination alters interfacial water structure in ways that may explain the unique hydrophobic properties of fluorinated materials.

papers.title: Frustration Quenching and Network Topology of the Energy Landscape as Primary Determinants of Protein-Ligand Binding Pose Prediction by Deep Learning Models.
papers.abstract: Deep learning co-folding and docking models accurately predict ligand binding poses at orthosteric sites yet systematically underperform at allosteric pockets. Here, we demonstrate that this accuracy gap reflects a fundamental biophysical property of local energy landscape topology-specifically, the magnitude of frustration quenching upon ligand binding-rather than an intrinsic algorithmic defect. By evaluating leading co-folding and docking paradigms across curated benchmarks and large-scale uncurated datasets, we show that AI prediction success strongly tracks frustration quenching-the degre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Deep learning models for protein-ligand pose prediction perform well at orthosteric sites but poorly at allosteric pockets. The authors show this gap is explained by a biophysical property of the binding site—the magnitude of frustration quenching upon ligand binding—rather than by algorithmic shortcomings, with prediction success tracking this energy-landscape feature across benchmarks.

papers.title: Fusion Peptide Insertion Configuration Determines the Mechanism of Membrane Curvature Induction in Human Parainfluenza Virus Type 3.
papers.abstract: Viral entry requires remodeling the host membrane with a short fusion peptide (FP) that anchors and deforms the target lipid bilayer. However, the contribution of the FP throughout the full fusion pathway remains unknown. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations define the membrane-deformation mechanisms associated with two distinct insertion configurations of membrane-bound human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV3) FP. Molecular simulations quantifying the linear response of curvature to the peptide are complemented with analyses of lipid organization and FP-lipid interactions to define t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to show that the human parainfluenza virus type 3 fusion peptide can insert into membranes in two distinct configurations, each producing membrane curvature through a different mechanism. By quantifying curvature response and lipid organization, the work reveals how insertion geometry dictates the physical pathway of membrane deformation during viral entry.

papers.title: Programming N-linked glycan composition through de novo protein design.
papers.abstract: N-linked glycans are ubiquitous post-translational modifications that mediate diverse biological processes, including cell signaling and adhesion, molecular recognition, and host-pathogen interactions. Despite their importance, N-linked glycans have largely remained beyond the reach of biomolecular design due to a lack of methods capable of jointly modeling glycans and protein structure. Here, we develop a general all-atom computational pipeline for creating de novo glycoproteins in which the amino acid sequence encodes both the location and composition of N-linked glycans. The method uses thr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed an all-atom computational pipeline for de novo design of glycoproteins where the protein sequence encodes both the location and composition of N-linked glycans. This enables programmable control over glycan attachment and composition, a capability previously beyond the reach of protein design due to the lack of methods jointly modeling glycans and protein structure.

papers.title: Unveiling the Molecular Driving Forces of Pollutant Extraction by Hydrophobic Eutectic Solvents.
papers.abstract: Hydrophobic eutectic solvents (HES) are emerging as sustainable alternatives to conventional organic solvents for the extraction of molecular pollutants from water. Yet, their selectivity remains poorly understood, hindering the predictive design of eutectic solvents beyond empirical success. Here, we present a multiscale strategy to rationalize and predict solute partitioning in HES. Focusing on bisphenol A (BPA) in trioctylphosphine oxide (TOPO):menthol as a prototypical system, we combine monophasic and biphasic molecular dynamics with quantum energy decomposition of dominant solvation moti
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses multiscale molecular dynamics simulations combined with quantum energy decomposition to explain why hydrophobic eutectic solvents selectively extract pollutants like bisphenol A from water, using the TOPO:menthol system as a model. The work identifies the dominant solvation interactions driving solute partitioning, offering a rational basis for designing eutectic solvents rather than relying on trial-and-error. It provides a predictive framework for tuning solvent selectivity in water treatment applications.

papers.title: Assessing the Competition between Bulk and Interfacial Nucleation of H2S Hydrates via Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms by which gas hydrates nucleate from aqueous solutions is essential for predicting and controlling their formation. Experimental observations have suggested that hydrate nucleation occurs preferentially at interfaces between the aqueous phase and hydrate-forming reservoirs. However, recent simulation studies have raised questions regarding the general validity of this assumption. Here, we investigate the spontaneous nucleation of H2S hydrates at 500 bar using molecular dynamics simulations employing the TIP4P/Ice water model and a four-site H2S potential, with the a
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This molecular dynamics study compares spontaneous nucleation of H2S hydrates in bulk aqueous solution versus at interfaces, using the TIP4P/Ice water model and a four-site H2S potential at 500 bar. The simulations test the common assumption that hydrate nucleation preferentially occurs at interfaces, finding conditions under which bulk nucleation competes with or dominates interfacial nucleation. The work clarifies when interface-driven nucleation is a general phenomenon versus a system-specific effect.

papers.title: A New Reactive Force Field for NOx-Water Interactions: Development, Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Peroxynitrite.
papers.abstract: Reactive nitrogen species (RNSs) are key contributors to plasma-liquid processes and play a critical role in the chemistry of plasma-activated water (PAW). Despite their importance, their molecular-level behavior in aqueous environments is still not well understood, largely due to the absence of reliable reactive force fields. In this study, a new ReaxFF parameter set, ReaxFFCHONx-2026, is developed and systematically assessed for modeling nitrogen- and oxygen-containing reactive species under both gas-phase and aqueous conditions relevant to plasma systems. The parameter set is optimized usin
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This paper develops a new reactive force field (ReaxFFCHONx-2026) for modeling reactive nitrogen species (RNS) in water, addressing a gap in molecular-level understanding of plasma-activated water chemistry. The parameter set is optimized and evaluated for gas-phase and aqueous conditions, then applied in molecular dynamics simulations of peroxynitrite. It provides a validated computational tool for studying NOx-water interactions relevant to plasma-liquid processes.

papers.title: Catalysis tuned for metabolic sensing: dynamics and mechanism of the RNA methyltransferase METTL16.
papers.abstract: The methyltransferase-like protein 16 (METTL16) is the writer enzyme that methylates adenosine to form N6-methyladenosine (m6A) on U6 spliceosomal RNA and MAT2A mRNA. The latter encodes the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of S-adenosyl methionine (SAM). Since methylation influences the stability of MAT2A mRNA, METTL16 is the sensor of SAM in the cell. Here, we investigate the (co)substrate recognition and catalytic mechanism of METTL16 by a combination of in vitro and simulation methods. We first solved the crystal structures of METTL16 in complex with bisubstrate analogs (BAs), conjugate
papers.summary: This study investigates how the RNA methyltransferase METTL16 recognizes its substrates and catalyzes m6A modification, using crystal structures with bisubstrate analogs combined with in vitro and computational approaches. METTL16 acts as a cellular SAM sensor by methylating MAT2A mRNA, thereby influencing its stability and SAM synthesis. The work reveals mechanistic details of substrate recognition and catalysis that underlie this metabolic sensing function.

papers.title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Galleria mellonella and Alphitobius diaperinus Protein Digestates Generated Using a Modified INFOGEST Protocol - In Vitro and In Silico Evidence.
papers.abstract: Insect-derived peptides have attracted increasing attention due to their potential health-promoting properties. This study investigated peptides released from Galleria mellonella (W) and Alphitobius diaperinus (B) proteins following a modified static INFOGEST protocol. Digestion-derived peptides were identified by LC-MS/MS and evaluated for anti-inflammatory activity using in vitro assays, bioinformatic prediction, and molecular docking, focusing on IKK-β as a key regulator of the NF-κB pathway. At 500 μg protein/mL, W-I2h and B-I2h reduced NF-κB reporter activity by 28.7% and 53.5%, respectiv
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
papers.summary: This study used a modified INFOGEST in vitro digestion protocol to release peptides from two edible insect species (Galleria mellonella and Alphitobius diaperinus), identified them by LC-MS/MS, and tested their anti-inflammatory activity. Peptide fractions reduced NF-κB reporter activity by up to 53.5%, with bioinformatic prediction and molecular docking suggesting IKK-β as a target. The work provides in vitro and in silico evidence that insect protein digestates contain immunomodulatory peptides.

papers.title: Ni-Decorated B12N12 Nanocages as High-Performance Platforms for Reversible NH3 Sensing: A Comprehensive DFT Study.
papers.abstract: Selective and reliable NH3 detection under realistic environmental conditions remains a major challenge for next-generation chemiresistive gas sensors. Herein, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to systematically investigate six Ni-decorated B12N12 nanocage configurations to identify the optimal active site for ammonia sensing. Among the investigated systems, Ni@b66 exhibited the best sensing performance, combining moderate adsorption strength (Eads = -0.82 eV), pronounced band-gap modulation (Δgap = 42.8%), and rapid recovery (τ = 3.74 s at 298 K). PDOS, ELF, CDD, and
papers.journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
papers.summary: This DFT study screens six configurations of Ni-decorated B12N12 nanocages for ammonia sensing and identifies Ni@b66 as the best candidate, showing moderate NH3 adsorption (-0.82 eV), a large band-gap change (42.8%), and fast recovery (3.74 s at room temperature). The work uses electronic-structure analysis to rationalize why this site gives strong, reversible sensing response, supporting Ni-decorated boron nitride nanocages as promising chemiresistive NH3 sensor materials.

papers.title: Experimental and Pharmacoinformatic Studies Reveal Allium cepa L. Extract-Mediated Modulation of Hepatitis B Virus Associated Inflammatory Pathways via Quercetin Glucoside Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health burden and often progresses to chronic liver inflammation, fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although current antiviral therapies effectively suppress viral replication, their ability to modulate HBV-associated complications remains limited. This study investigates the HBV-associated antiviral and host modulatory potential of methanolic extract of Allium cepa bulb (AC) using integrated in vitro and computational approaches. Cytotoxicity, reverse transcriptase inhibition, time- and dose-dependent inhibition of HBsAg and HBeAg
papers.summary: This study combines in vitro experiments with computational (pharmacoinformatic) analyses to show that a methanolic extract of onion (Allium cepa) bulb inhibits hepatitis B virus reverse transcriptase and reduces secretion of viral antigens HBsAg and HBeAg in a dose- and time-dependent manner. The authors attribute this activity to quercetin glucoside derivatives and propose that these compounds modulate HBV-associated inflammatory pathways through host-directed mechanisms. The work is preliminary, relying largely on in vitro and docking-type predictions without in vivo validation.

papers.title: Structure-Transport Relationships in Aqueous Fructose Solutions: A Combined Molecular Dynamics and NMR Diffusion Study.
papers.abstract: Fructose is widely used in the food industry and is proposed as a sustainable biomass feedstock for chemical manufacturing. Upon dissolution in water, it undergoes mutarotation into different tautomers, primarily β-d-fructopyranose (68%) and β-d-fructofuranose (22%), as well as into the linear keto d-fructose structure. Although present only in small amounts, the linear tautomer may alter diffusion within aqueous media and porous catalytic materials. To elucidate the structure-transport properties of aqueous solutions containing fructose, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are combined with n
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with NMR diffusion measurements to investigate how the different tautomers of fructose (β-fructopyranose, β-fructofuranose, and the linear keto form) affect molecular transport in aqueous solution. The authors find that even the minor linear tautomer can influence diffusion behavior, which has implications for using fructose as a biomass feedstock in catalytic processes. The work provides a detailed structure-transport relationship for aqueous fructose solutions.

papers.title: Impact of Inhibitor Size and Flexibility on the Binding Pathways to c-Src Kinase.
papers.abstract: The conformational plasticity of protein kinases poses a challenge for inhibitor design, motivating the use of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study their dynamic binding processes. While conformational changes are increasingly discussed, the impact of drug compound flexibility remains underexplored because of experimental limitations. In this study, we employ two-dimensional replica-exchange MD simulations to investigate how c-Src kinase binds to PP1, a small inhibitor, and to dasatinib, a larger, more flexible inhibitor. Simulations totaling 600 μs revealed frequent binding and unbind
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.summary: Using 600 μs of two-dimensional replica-exchange molecular dynamics, the authors compared how c-Src kinase binds the small inhibitor PP1 versus the larger, more flexible dasatinib. The simulations revealed frequent binding and unbinding events, showing that inhibitor size and flexibility shape the binding pathways and the kinase's conformational plasticity. This clarifies how drug properties influence target engagement at the molecular level.

papers.title: Molecular dynamics analysis of T567 phosphorylation-induced conformational changes in ezrin.
papers.abstract: Ezrin, a key member of the ERM (Ezrin-Radixin-Moesin) family, links the plasma membrane to the actin cytoskeleton and is regulated by a conformational switch between closed and open states. Although phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate binding and phosphorylation at Thr567 are known to promote Ezrin activation, the associated conformational mechanism remains incompletely understood. Here, we combined Martini coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations with enhanced sampling, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA calculations to compare wild-type Ezrin with the phosphomimetic
papers.summary: This study uses coarse-grained and all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how phosphorylation at Thr567 drives ezrin from its closed to open conformation. The phosphomimetic mutant is compared to wild-type ezrin, revealing the structural changes that underlie ezrin activation and membrane-cytoskeleton linkage. The work provides mechanistic insight into ERM protein regulation at atomic resolution.

papers.title: Context-dependent protein structure prediction analysis and complex stoichiometry inference with MultimerMapper.
papers.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed the field of structural biology, notably with the accuracy level reached by AlphaFold in the prediction of protein structures. While cloud implementations have broadened access to these methods, there is still a lack of non-AI tools to systematically interpret and analyze the resulting data, especially under varying modeling contexts. Here, we present MultimerMapper, a pipeline and software suite designed to generate, extract, integrate, analyze, and visualize the behavior of multimeric systems in ensembles of overlapping protein struct
papers.summary: MultimerMapper is a new software pipeline that systematically generates, extracts, integrates, analyzes, and visualizes multimeric protein structure predictions across ensembles of overlapping models, addressing the gap in non-AI tools for interpreting AlphaFold-style outputs under varying modeling contexts. It also enables inference of complex stoichiometry from these structural ensembles, helping researchers make sense of context-dependent prediction behavior.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration reveals the role of PFOS in sarcopenia via ESRRG and RBP4: from computational prediction to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) has been shown to cause multi-organ dysfunction; however, the specific mechanisms underlying its association with sarcopenia remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with computational prediction and experimental validation to investigate how exposure to PFOS, a persistent environmental pollutant, contributes to sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss). The authors identify ESRRG and RBP4 as key mediators of PFOS-associated muscle dysfunction, providing mechanistic insight into an environmental risk factor for sarcopenia.

papers.title: Case Report: Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula as adjunctive therapy for leptospirosis with Weil's syndrome.
papers.abstract: Leptospirosis is a global zoonotic disease with over one million cases annually worldwide. Approximately 5%-10% of patients progress to Weil's syndrome, characterized by multi-organ failure and high mortality, but treatment options remain limited. This report describes a patient with severe leptospirosis who showed marked improvement following treatment with Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula (LXJDHYF), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, and explores potential mechanisms.
papers.summary: This case report describes a single patient with severe leptospirosis complicated by Weil's syndrome (multi-organ failure) who showed marked clinical improvement after receiving a traditional Chinese medicine formula, Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula, as an adjunct to standard care. The authors also speculate on possible mechanisms underlying the observed benefit. As a single case report, the work is hypothesis-generating only and cannot establish efficacy or causality.

papers.title: Multi-source data integration and ensemble machine learning analysis of the role of Corilagin in regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress and alleviating intestinal ischemia reperfusion injury in mice.
papers.abstract: Intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IIRI) is driven by oxidative stress, excessive inflammation, Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress (ERS), and disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier. Corilagin, a natural ellagitannin with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, has shown protective effects against IIRI; however, its cross-species and multitarget mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-source data and ensemble machine learning to investigate how Corilagin, a natural compound, protects against intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice by regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress. The work identifies cross-species, multi-target mechanisms underlying the compound's protective effects on oxidative stress, inflammation, and intestinal barrier integrity.

papers.title: Exploring molecular interactions between yeast topoisomerase I and RNA polymerase III subunit, Rpc82 using an in-silico approach.
papers.abstract: The process of DNA transcription leads to the generation of torsional stress, which must be resolved for smooth progression of the transcription machinery. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, DNA topoisomerase I (Top I), a type IB topoisomerase, plays a critical role in relaxing supercoils and mitigating the topological strain associated with transcription. While several proteins from the transcription machinery have been reported to interact with yeast Top I, the precise structural domains involved and the detailed features of the interaction interfaces remain largely unexplored. This gap is partly
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics simulations to model how yeast topoisomerase I (Top I) interacts with Rpc82, a subunit of RNA polymerase III. The authors identify putative interaction interfaces and structural domains that may mediate this binding, proposing a model for how Top I is recruited to relieve torsional stress during transcription. The findings are computational predictions that require experimental validation.

papers.title: In silico evaluation of potential penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2) inhibitors from Borassus flabellifer haustorium against cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
papers.abstract: The emergence of cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains, encoding altered Penicillin-Binding Protein 2 (PBP2), has become a major global public health concern. The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial agents. In the present study, phytocompounds derived from the haustorium of Borassus flabellifer L. were investigated as potential inhibitors of PBP2 using an integrated in silico approach.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and related in silico methods to screen phytochemicals from the haustorium of the palm Borassus flabellifer as potential inhibitors of penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2) in cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The work identifies candidate compounds with predicted binding affinity to the altered PBP2 target, proposing them as starting points for novel antimicrobial development against drug-resistant gonorrhea. Findings are computational only and require experimental validation.
